mif_rows.row_name: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, on first exposure to the departure maneuver, could not follow the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures without assistance, and the IP directed the exit point and the climb routing. Exit heading diverged by 15 degrees from the predetermined course before the IP intervened. Performance met the desired code for this block but was marginal within it; a working knowledge of the Local Area Procedures departure routing before the next sortie is expected to reduce the direction required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP followed the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures and directed the A/C to the assigned flight area, requiring only the IP's verbal prompts at the exit point. Altitude at level off reached a 300 feet deviation and was corrected with delay after the prompt, without IP intervention on the controls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP performed the VFR departure, climb and level off while heading to the flight area without any verbal prompt from the IP. Airspeed in the climb deviated by 15 knots and exit heading by 8 degrees, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP followed the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures with accuracy and directed the A/C safely to the assigned flight area over the predetermined route. Level off was completed within 90 feet of the assigned altitude, exit heading was held within 4 degrees and no adjacent area was entered. Area entry was reported at the assigned point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP applied the departure technique of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the Local Area Procedures without any prompt, keeping the A/C on the predetermined course throughout the transition to the flight area. Deviations were negligible, with level off within 40 feet of the assigned altitude, airspeed within 3 knots and exit heading within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to an incorrect climb technique in which power and pitch were set before the departure turn was established, did not follow the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures. The A/C diverged 20 degrees from the predetermined course and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 450 feet, with the result that the IP directed the turn back to the route and executed part of the level off. Further study of the Local Area Procedures departure routing is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to lack of awareness of the A/C position relative to the flight area boundary, did not direct the A/C safely to the assigned flight area and continued the transition toward an adjacent area. The IP took control of the routing before the boundary was crossed, at a point where the track error had already reached 18 degrees from the predetermined course. Review of the area boundaries and of the assigned entry points before the next sortie is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP followed the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures and reached the assigned flight area, but completed the climb and level off only after the IP's verbal prompts on the departure course. Altitude at level off reached a 300 feet deviation and was corrected with delay, without IP intervention on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section; earlier recognition of the level off point is expected to improve over the following departures.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP performed the VFR departure and the climb to the flight area without any verbal prompt from the IP, remaining on the predetermined course. Airspeed in the climb deviated by 16 knots and altitude at level off by 200 feet, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP followed the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures with accuracy and speed and directed the A/C safely to the assigned flight area without any prompt. Level off was completed within 100 feet of the assigned altitude, airspeed was held within 8 knots and exit heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP executed the departure maneuver in a standardized manner in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the Local Area Procedures, with continuous cross-check between the performance instruments and the A/C position over the predetermined route. Deviations were negligible, with level off within 30 feet of the assigned altitude, airspeed within 3 knots and exit heading within 2 degrees, and no adjacent area was entered. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to a departure technique that held a fixed pitch attitude without reference to the climb airspeed schedule, did not perform the climb and level off prescribed for the transition to the flight area. Airspeed in the climb diverged by 28 knots and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 500 feet, with the result that the IP directed the pitch and power corrections and executed part of the level off. Further practice of the departure climb profile is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to poor workload distribution, with the departure frequency change, the navigation to the area entry point and the climb attempted at the same time, did not follow the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures. The A/C left the predetermined route by 22 degrees and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 400 feet before the IP intervened and directed the recovery to the route. The assigned area was reached only after the IP had re-established the routing. Shedding of the secondary task until the climb is established is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to late selection of the departure course after the traffic pattern exit, did not maintain the predetermined route to the assigned flight area. Exit heading reached a 10 degrees deviation and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt, with the result that the area entry point was reached late, without IP intervention on the controls. Earlier selection of the departure course is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to distraction by departure radio traffic during the climb, did not check the performance instrument indications against the A/C position over the predetermined route. Altitude at level off reached a 300 feet deviation, recognized and corrected with delay only after the IP's verbal prompt. Priority to the climb profile over the secondary radio task is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP performed the VFR departure and the transition to the assigned flight area within the desired standards, without IP's intervention. Airspeed in the climb deviated twice by up to 15 knots and exit heading by 7 degrees, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section; steadier control of the climb airspeed schedule through the departure turn is expected to improve.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP followed the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures accurately and directed the A/C safely to the assigned flight area over the predetermined route, without any prompt. Level off was completed within 120 feet of the assigned altitude, airspeed within 9 knots and exit heading within 5 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP executed the departure maneuver and the transition to the flight area in an impeccable and standardized manner, with continuous cross-check of the control and performance instruments against the assigned route. Deviations were negligible, with level off within 50 feet of the assigned altitude, airspeed within 4 knots and exit heading within 2 degrees, and the area entry call was made at the assigned point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to an incorrect level off technique in which the power reduction was initiated at the assigned altitude instead of the lead point, did not perform the climb and level off prescribed for the transition to the flight area. The assigned altitude was exceeded by 550 feet and airspeed diverged by 30 knots, with the result that the IP took control and executed the recovery to the assigned altitude. The transition to the flight area continued under IP direction. Further practice of the level off lead point and of the power schedule is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the A/C position relative to the assigned flight area after the unplanned change of the departure routing, did not direct the A/C safely to the assigned flight area. The A/C crossed into an adjacent area without authorization at a track error of 25 degrees from the predetermined course, and the IP directed the return to the assigned area. Review of the area boundaries and of the Local Area Procedures departure routes is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to a trim technique that was not completed after the gear and flap retraction, did not maintain the climb airspeed schedule during the transition to the flight area. Airspeed reached a 20 knots deviation and was corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompt, without IP intervention on the controls. Completion of the trim before the departure turn is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to attention captured by a caution indication during the departure climb while the A/C state went unmonitored, did not check the performance instrument indications against the A/C position over the predetermined route. Exit heading reached a 10 degrees deviation and altitude at level off a 300 feet deviation, both recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Maintaining the cross-check while a secondary indication is worked is required.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to a bank angle in the traffic pattern exit turn greater than the one prescribed by the Local Area Procedures, did not roll out on the predetermined departure course. Exit heading deviated by 8 degrees and altitude at level off by 220 feet, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Use of the briefed bank angle for the exit turn is expected to place the roll out on course.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP, due to complacency in a familiar departure that replaced an active cross-check, did not compare the performance instrument indications with the A/C position during the climb to the flight area. Airspeed deviated by 14 knots and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 180 feet at level off, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. No adjacent area was entered and the area entry call was made at the assigned point. An active scan of the departure routing is expected on every sortie, however familiar the profile.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP followed the local traffic pattern exit - departure procedures and directed the A/C safely to the assigned flight area within the desired standards, without prompt or intervention from the IP. Level off was completed within 140 feet of the assigned altitude and exit heading was held within 5 degrees, at the edge of the desired band. Marginal performance for the Training Section; tighter control of the level off lead point is expected to improve over the following departures.

observations.mif_row: VFR Departure / Transition to Flight Areas
observations.text: SP executed the departure maneuver and the transition to the assigned flight area in an impeccable and standardized manner, applying the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the Local Area Procedures without any prompt. Deviations were negligible, with level off within 40 feet of the assigned altitude, airspeed within 3 knots and exit heading within 2 degrees, and no adjacent area was entered. Above end of block MIF achieved.
